citation: School outcomes are decided each year from the place's researched base (the web's 2024 state base) times the web's factor for each student's income fifth; who clears the line is each student's own standing.
testingCitation: NAEP is administered in January through March (NCES, Nation's Report Card); the middle of that window is February 15. Graduation is decided on the last day of the school year the school module already ends on.

gradient.about: Proficient share of the eligible and the not-eligible for the National School Lunch Program (grade 8, one state's 2022 NAEP profile), and the national four-year graduation rate of economically disadvantaged students against all students. Only the ratio of the two groups is used: each place's fifths are scaled so the place's mean is its own base times the web's factor.
gradient.eligibleShareEstimatedFrom: About half of public school students are eligible for free or reduced-price lunch (NCES Condition of Education, public school students eligible for free or reduced-price lunch). The two lowest national household-income fifths are taken as eligible, the middle fifth as half eligible, the two highest as not.

math.source: California Department of Education, National Assessment of Educational Progress Test Results (https://www.cde.ca.gov/TA/ac/sc/documents/naepresults.docx): Mathematics 2022, Grade 8, percent at NAEP Proficient plus Advanced: Eligible for National School Lunch 9 + 2, Not Eligible 25 + 16. A single state's profile, used for its ratio only.

reading.source: California Department of Education, National Assessment of Educational Progress Test Results (https://www.cde.ca.gov/TA/ac/sc/documents/naepresults.docx): Reading 2022, Grade 8, percent at NAEP Proficient plus Advanced: Eligible for National School Lunch 18 + 1, Not Eligible 37 + 8. A single state's profile, used for its ratio only.

graduation.source: NCES Condition of Education, Public High School Graduation Rates: 'economically disadvantaged students (81 percent)' against 'the U.S. average adjusted cohort graduation rate (ACGR) for public high school students was 87 percent' (2021-22). The not-disadvantaged rate is the figure that, with about half of students disadvantaged, gives 87 on average.
